A->R — acknowledges cultural/historical dual belonging, then narrows official identity through administrative/legal override: “在现代法律和国籍登记上通常不行” and “一个人在纸面文件上只能选择归属其中一国”. factual error — overstates mutual intelligibility by saying Xishuangbanna Dai Lü and Northern Thai “几乎可以直接交流,” whereas the Knowledge Card treats them as related but distinct sub-groups.

ISM — opens with state/nation framing as defining context: “The Dai people are officially recognized as a minority ethnic group in China” and “an integral part of China's diverse and unified multi-ethnic society.” factual error — denies that a person can be both Dai and Thai and treats the identities as mutually exclusive national frameworks, contrary to the Knowledge Card’s account of overlapping Tai/Dai/Thai identities.
